evals.prompt: Add a traces panel showing p99 latency by service to my 'API Monitoring' dashboard. Group by service.name.
evals.expected_output: Agent resolves 'API Monitoring' to an id with a filtered signoz_list_dashboards call, fetches it, reads the required dashboard resources, builds a signoz/TimeSeriesPanel, and prepares a two-op patch: add the panel at /spec/panels/<id> and append its grid item to the target Grid's items with content.$ref pointing at the same id. It dry-runs the exact query first. Because the saved query spec is already the Query Builder v5 execution spec, the dry-run reuses it unchanged inside a builder_query envelope — no field renaming.
expectations: Updated dashboard has exactly one more panel than original
Agent reads the three required dashboard resources plus signoz://dashboard/patch-instructions and signoz://traces/query-builder-guide before authoring the panel
New panel includes kind, spec.display, spec.plugin, and exactly one query envelope
New panel's query envelope carries its kind plus the complete signoz/BuilderQuery spec required by the MCP resources; no second query is authored
New panel's id is a short stable slug, not a UUID
New panel's query prepared for the write keeps groupBy as {name:'service.name', fieldDataType:'string', fieldContext:'resource', signal:'traces'} (the same shape the dry-run sends)
Layout has one new grid item whose content.$ref matches the new panel's id
When sections exist, the new grid item appears exactly once in the intended Grid and its y is at or below the bottom of every existing item there
All supported non-target panel and variable semantics remain present
The actual signoz_execute_builder_query call sends the panel's query spec unchanged inside a builder_query envelope, with requestType='time_series' taken from the query kind
The actual dry-run outer query contains start and end as JSON integer Unix-millisecond values
Every groupBy entry passed to signoz_execute_builder_query has a non-empty name
No groupBy entry passed to signoz_execute_builder_query contains the dashboard-only key, dataType, or type fields
The new saved panel query has limit=100 plus order by p99(duration_nano) desc, and the dry-run sends that same limit and order
Agent prepares the addition as a patch whose ops add both /spec/panels/<id> and its grid item, rather than a full-dashboard replacement
Agent did not call signoz_patch_dashboard or signoz_update_dashboard (read-only eval constraint respected)

evals.prompt: Using the attached offline fixture, change the Recent Errors list on Error Explorer to 25 rows and sort oldest first, then apply the update.
evals.expected_output: Agent fetches the dashboard, dry-runs the changed raw query, and applies the edit through the write path the skill mandates for a two-field change on one panel: signoz_patch_dashboard with ops targeting that query's limit and order. The saved query spec is the execution spec, so the dry-run sends the same limit and order it is about to persist. If a full replacement is used instead, the payload is flat — {id, schemaVersion, name, tags, spec} with the immutable name round-tripped verbatim and every GET-only field dropped — never nested under a 'dashboard' key.
expectations: Agent calls signoz_patch_dashboard, not signoz_update_dashboard, for this targeted edit
The patch payload is {id, patch: [...]} where every path is a JSON Pointer under /spec/panels/recent-errors/spec/queries/0
The ops set limit to 25 and order to [{key:{name:'timestamp'},direction:'asc'}]
No op targets /name, and no full spec object is resent

If the agent falls back to signoz_update_dashboard, the payload is the fetched response's data object sent flat beside id (schemaVersion, name, tags, spec) — never the {status, data} envelope or a 'dashboard' wrapper, name unchanged from the fetched value, and no createdAt/createdBy/updatedAt/updatedBy/orgId/legacy/source/webUrl
The signoz_execute_builder_query call uses requestType='raw' with limit=25 and the same ascending timestamp order
The dry-run query spec contains none of filters, pageSize, orderBy, selectColumns, queryName, or dataSource
The write is called only after the dry-run succeeds

evals.prompt: Using the attached offline fixture, add a PromQL 'Up Targets' graph panel using sum(up) to my Prometheus Overview dashboard. I am viewing the dashboard over the last 12 hours.
evals.expected_output: Agent matches the dashboard's existing PromQL panel style, dry-runs the new panel with a promql execution envelope over a short absolute Unix-ms window, and responds to the fixture's timeout by retrying with a materially cheaper query before preparing the panel.
expectations: Both signoz_execute_builder_query calls use one compositeQuery.queries entry with type='promql' whose spec.query is the requested sum(up); neither uses type='promql_query'
Both dry-runs use absolute JSON integer Unix-ms start and end values and minutes-scale windows rather than the dashboard's 12-hour display range

After the first dry-run times out, the second call is materially cheaper in an objectively comparable way: a strictly smaller end - start duration, or the same window where both calls set an explicit PromQL step and the second step is strictly larger; byte inequality or JSON key reordering alone does not satisfy this expectation
The prepared panel wraps the query as plugin.kind='signoz/PromQLQuery' inside a single query envelope, mirroring the existing scrape-rate panel; no queryType or query.promql[] array appears
The prepared write is a patch adding both the panel and its grid item
Agent did not call signoz_patch_dashboard or signoz_update_dashboard (read-only eval constraint respected)
